concepts.def: Kaiser Wilhelm II gave up the throne in Nov 1918
First Weimar President, Social Democrat leader
Emergency law letting the President rule by decree
Seats matched to share of votes — many parties

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 9 November 1918 Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated as Germany lost WWI.

The Social Democrat leader Friedrich Ebert took charge. Germany became a republic. Two days later, the war ended.

In August 1919 Germany got a new constitution.

All adults over 20 could vote. The Reichstag was elected by proportional representation. A President was elected separately — and held emergency power under Article 48.

The Treaty of Versailles in June 1919 forced Germany to accept war guilt.

It lost 13% of its land, all colonies, most of its army and owed huge reparations. Many Germans called it a 'Diktat' — a forced peace.
